Subject: Privacy & DPA follow-up — SCC selection and controller/processor alignment

Hi Lena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) GDPR / DPA / SCCs
- You indicated FinServe will act as the Controller for the product data in scope. Please confirm if that remains correct for all use cases discussed (transactional customer data + analytics).
- From Redwood's side we typically sign a Controller->Processor DPA and adopt the Controller-to-Processor SCC set. If you prefer Processor->Processor wording please flag and we’ll escalate internally.

2) SOC 2 / security evidence
- FinServe asked for a SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period) plus some high-level notes on encryption (at-rest / in-transit) and subprocessor list. We can provide a secure link for SOC 2 access.

3) Vendor security questionnaire
- You mentioned emailing over your vendor security questionnaire. Please send the completed file and any required evidence. We’ll task the security/legal team to review and aim for a 48–72 hour turnaround for the initial pass.

4) DPA redlines and timing
- If you can share any redlines to our DPA (or we can send our template + suggested redlines) we’ll align legal and return a passthrough. Typical turnaround for commercial templates is ~2 business days, subject to complexity.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm Controller role and upload the filled questionnaire + any preferred DPA redlines (if available) to the HubSpot deal link (or reply with attachments).
- Us: we’ll provide SOC 2 access link, send our DPA template and a recommended Controller->Processor SCC selection, and have Legal (Neha) + SE (Vivek) review questionnaire.

Attaching an empty DPA template and a short checklist for reference. If helpful we can schedule a 20-min legal kickoff next week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping — quick legal/security read: 

1) SCC selection
- Controller->Processor SCC language is our standard approach for customer relationships where the customer controls personal data. I’m comfortable recommending we proceed with that as the primary option.
- If FinServe insists on Processor->Processor wording we should get a clear business justification and escalate to GC; that is less common and requires additional safeguards.

2) DPA redlines (initial guidance)
- I will prepare a redline against our standard DPA focusing on: data subject rights cooperation, limited subprocessing, security obligations (SOC2 + encryption), breach notification SLA (72 hours), and data deletion/return at contract end.
- I’m attaching a redline draft: Redwood_DPA_redline_ForFinServe.docx (internal). Please do not share the internal draft externally until final.

3) Evidence request / SOC2
- We will provide a secure SOC 2 access link (not a public copy) and a one-pager on encryption/key management. Provide those to FinServe security mailbox and via the HubSpot deal link.

Turnaround: I’ll aim to get an internal redline to you by end of day Monday (2026-06-15). Legal will take a look at the vendor questionnaire and flag anything high-risk in the initial pass within 48 business hours.

Recommended next step: Karthik, please send the DPA template to Lena and let them know Legal will follow with a redline. Vivek, can you prepare the SOC2 link + encryption summary and send to security@finserve.com?

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
